name: ramp_get_attention_feed
description:
Return the authenticated user's homepage attention feed.

Use this tool to see what needs the user's attention right now: pending approvals,
missing receipts, overdue reviews, signatures, and similar action items that appear
on the Ramp homepage.

By default, the tool returns the default homepage sections with compact
LIST-hydrated task rows. To fetch more from a section, pass that section's
section_type and next_cursor back in sections.

For own-card GET_ATTENTION_FEED remediation, use this as the canonical task feed.
blocking_effects describes a task type's possible sanction, not proof that an item
caused the active lock. Use browser_handoff for user action in Ramp. For an
available CompleteTransactionRevision, inspect or edit the transaction and call
it with a nonblank reason. Re-read both tools and continue relevant overdue tasks;
success requires the task absent, blocking_task_count=0, and is_spendable=true.
Pending verification is not an unlock.

name: ramp_get_funds
description:
Retrieve funds (cards or budgets) and their balances, restrictions, locks, owners,
or permitted spend. For a named person's funds, resolve their UUID with GetOrgChart
and pass user_uuids. For the current user's funds, use MY_FUNDS. Search by fund name
with search_by_fund_display_name or look up a known UUID with fund_uuid.

Every fund includes balance_data. Treat its remaining amount as authoritative for cleared
charges, pending authorizations, and applicable rollover. limit_amount excludes rollover;
accrued_rollover_amount is the opening carry, already included in remaining_amount.
Do not add rollover or subtract spending again. Never infer that
a booking is included merely because it is confirmed: a postpaid booking with no charge or
pending authorization is a future charge and has not yet reduced the remaining balance.

A fund with a lock can't be spent from until it is unlocked, even though it is ACTIVE
and keeps its remaining amount. Never present a locked fund as available; mention it
separately with its lock reason, without quoting its remaining amount as money left
unless the user asks what it holds once unlocked. A member lock blocks only that member.

Set True to return only funds that are active AND have virtual cards enabled — the only funds an agent card can be minted on. Set False to return the funds that cannot. Leave unset to return funds regardless of agent-card eligibility. Every returned fund also carries an `agent_card_eligible` flag.

Use ALL_FUNDS for general searches (e.g., searching by fund name) or when no specific owner is mentioned. NEVER use this parameter when the user mentions a specific person - use user_uuids instead.

name: ramp_reporting_query
description:
Query reporting data and return aggregate or individual-record rows.
Use for analysis or validation. Does not save reports.

Use exact catalog dimension/measure names and kinds, not display labels.
For SQL, groupable=false (also needs.groupable=false) detail fields need
dimensions without measures; query totals separately.
Catalog filters need filterable=true, ops from supported_filter_ops, and
values matching filter_value_kind. Search tags need resolved IDs with
original types, not names.
Financial-statement datasets accept `statement.time_window`, optional
provider-dimension `statement.filters`, and a response-size `limit`. They
return fixed, canonically ordered account and calculated-total rows with
provider currency and publication metadata. These overlapping rows must
not be summed. SQL controls, comparisons, and top-N scope are unsupported;
missing or changed ledger publications return a failed-precondition error.

For SQL datasets, a `filters` clause whose
`field` is a catalog field is a row predicate; one whose `field` is a
selected measure output name (its `name` alias when present) is the
preferred aggregate predicate and applies after grouping (HAVING), e.g.
`{"field": "txn_count", "op": "gt", "value": 3}`. `having` and
`aggregate_filters` remain supported equivalents, but are deprecated and
migrated into `filters`; `result_metadata.predicate_migration` records the
migration.
Order by any selected orderable dimension or measure output.

For complete SQL results, set `page_size` (1–1,000) to paginate. Pass
`response.table.page.next` as `start` with the same `report_query`,
`query_scope`, and `page_size` until it is null. Pages read live data, not
a snapshot. Financial statements and `second_stage` / `post_aggregation`
queries do not support pagination.

A measure ref may carry its own `filters` plus a unique `name` to emit a
conditional aggregate column ("sumIf"). Select the same measure several
times with different filters for side-by-side cohort columns, e.g. one
spend total per category grouped by user, including an "other" column via
a NOT_IN filter. Measure filters use the same field/op/value shape as
query filters but only base-dataset fields.
A catalog entry with non-empty `aggregations` also accepts a ref with
`agg` (`type` from `aggregations`) and a required `name`. If `covered_by`
lists a measure for that agg, select that measure instead.
Use `second_stage` whenever the question aggregates per-group results
again (days/months/vendors per X, average monthly spend per X, highest or
lowest month per X, users over $X per month): retain `dimensions` and
compute `measures`, each `{"agg": SUM|AVG|MIN|MAX|COUNT, "of":
<first-stage measure output name or null>, "name"}`, across the collapsed
groups, instead of post-processing first-stage rows yourself. COUNT
without `of` counts groups that survive the aggregate predicates (a
measure-output `filters` clause or the deprecated forms, which migrate
like any other query); only a stage made solely of such counts needs a
predicate, so never add a threshold just to satisfy it when
SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX or COUNT of an operand is present. For example, select
user plus `{"field": "spend_date", "time_grain": "day"}`, filter
daily_spend over $500, then use `{"dimensions": ["user"], "measures":
[{"agg": "COUNT", "name": "days_over_limit"}]}`; retain `spend_date`
instead to count users over the threshold per day or month. For average
monthly spend per vendor, select vendor and month with `{"measure":
"amount", "name": "monthly_spend"}` and use `{"agg": "AVG", "of":
"monthly_spend", "name": "avg_monthly_spend"}`: an average of monthly
totals over the months that have spend (a month with no rows is not a
zero), so present it as an average per active month or add a COUNT of
months; MIN/MAX of the same operand give each vendor's lowest and highest
month. Operands must be selected first-stage measure outputs (aliases
allowed), never window measures. Order by retained dimensions or stage
names only; `limit` applies to the final rows; no `totals`. Use user with
amount for employee spend; only per-diem or meal questions need attendee
with amount_per_attendee, which allocates across Ramp employee attendees
only (external attendees are excluded) and falls back to the spending
employee when no attendee list exists. Keep the daily grain so day counts
are by UTC calendar day. `post_aggregation` (`{"dimension", "name"}`) is
the deprecated equivalent of a single COUNT stage; do not use it for new
queries.

Use `max_groups` for K named values plus Other independently on every
selected non-time dimension, retaining all time buckets. Set
`ranking_order_by` to selected first-stage measure scores. When the time
range is omitted, ranking covers all authorized data. Display `order_by`
is separate. Omit `limit`; without `page_size`, ranked results have a
1,000-row cap disclosed through result_metadata.is_truncated. Ranking
cannot combine with aggregate predicates or second_stage.

Covers Ramp data and canonical financial statements from authorized connected ERP books. Data is eventually consistent (may lag a few minutes).

query_scope.title: query_scope
query_scope.description: Result-set scope. Use complete for all, each, every, or otherwise unrestricted results. Omit report_query.limit; complete overrides any supplied flat limit and uses 1000 rows per response unless page_size enables pagination. Use complete with max_groups; it preserves per-dimension ranking. Use top_n only when the user explicitly requested exactly N rows, and set report_query.limit to that N. Financial statements do not support top_n; complete preserves their canonical order. Omission preserves the query limit.

agg.description: Optional query-time aggregation; measure then names a base-dataset field or catalog measure whose record values are aggregated. agg.type must be one of that entry's catalog aggregations; QUANTILE_NUMERIC also needs agg.percentile. Requires name.

items.description:
Reference to a dataset measure, optionally restricted by filters.

``filters`` make the measure conditional ("sum of amount WHERE category =
X") without restricting the query's row set or any other selected
measure. This is how one query produces side-by-side conditional columns,
e.g. per-category spend totals grouped by employee. Filtered refs must set
``name`` so each output column has a distinct, addressable name.

``agg`` makes ``measure`` name a base-dataset field or catalog measure
whose record values are aggregated at query time, e.g. the median of
``amount``. The catalog lists the aggregations each entry accepts.

items.description:
One aggregate over the first-stage groups collapsed into a retained grain.

Operands are first-stage group values, so every group weighs one: ``AVG``
of a first-stage measure is an average of groups, not the raw-row average,
and only groups that exist count. A time bucket with no rows is absent,
not zero, so ``AVG`` over months is an average per active month.

second_stage.description: Optional second aggregation stage over the first-stage groups: retain `dimensions` ([] for one scalar row; otherwise selected first-stage dimensions; at least one other selected dimension is collapsed) and compute `measures`, each `{agg: SUM|AVG|MIN|MAX|COUNT, of: <first-stage measure output name or null>, name, display_name}`, across the collapsed groups. Each first-stage group weighs once: COUNT without `of` counts qualifying groups (and then requires an aggregate predicate); AVG is an average of existing groups, so AVG over months is per active month (a month with no rows is absent, not zero). Aggregate predicates on first-stage outputs qualify groups before this stage. Mutually exclusive with post_aggregation and max_groups; comparison requires `dimensions: []`.

name: ramp_search_bills
description:
Search submitted and active draft bills by invoice number, payee, payment ID, or UUID.

Returns summary records for submitted and active draft bills, including
authoritative lifecycle information: is_draft=true means an unsubmitted
draft; is_draft=false means a submitted bill. Full bill details are outside
this lookup contract. Accepts a UUID even when its lifecycle is unknown.
Submitted and active draft bills may both be returned unless filters exclude
them; include_drafts=False restricts results to submitted bills. Archived
bills are excluded by default; set include_archived=true to include them. An
unpaid bill or one awaiting approval is not necessarily a draft.
Explicit invoice references use invoice_number for exact matching, including
one- or two-character numbers; query remains a partial text search or UUID lookup.
exact_amount filters the recorded invoice header total in its original currency
before pagination. Drafts without a header amount cannot match; this is not a
computed line-item total or remaining balance.
Repeat the same filters with page_cursor until next_page_cursor is null; a page
is not the complete match set. No date restriction applies unless supplied.
Results include can_view_payment_details: false means the payment-detail
lookup is unavailable for this user. Null means access is unknown, not denied.
Access may change after search and is checked again when details are requested.
Search results do not include payment status, approval status, or payment
date; those fields are null here and are available from the bill details
lookup for a specific bill. status_summary and paid_date reflect the bill's
lifecycle and payment state.

include_paid.description: Optional payment-status filter. Leave unset for UUID lookups when the bill's lifecycle is unknown. False restricts results to open submitted bills and excludes drafts. If include_drafts=true, this filter is skipped, so paid submitted bills remain eligible. When unset, no payment-status filter is applied.

invoice_number.title: invoice_number
invoice_number.description: Optional exact invoice number. Use for an explicit invoice reference, including short numbers like '48'. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; case, punctuation, and leading zeros are preserved. '48' does not match '148' or 'INV-48'. When query is nonempty, both filters must match (AND). Invoice numbers are not unique across vendors: all accessible matches are returned with normal lifecycle filters and pagination.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Maximum number of bills to return (max 50)

page_cursor.title: page_cursor
page_cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's next_page_cursor. The only valid string values are encrypted cursor tokens from a previous response (long strings starting with 'gAAAAA'). For the first page, for no more results, or for anything that is not one of those encrypted tokens, pass None (never the string 'None').

query.title: query
query.description: Optional invoice number, payee name, payment ID, or bill UUID. Queries of 3+ characters use partial matching (e.g. 'UPS' finds 'UPS Store' and '1722' finds 'INV-1722'). Shorter queries (e.g. '3D') match the exact payee name only. For an explicit invoice number, use invoice_number for exact matching instead. A UUID performs an exact lookup across submitted and draft bills. Do not use this for due-date concepts like 'past due' or 'due next week'; use from_due_date/to_due_date instead.

status_summaries.title: status_summaries
status_summaries.description:
Filter bills by one or more detailed status summaries. Returns bills whose status matches ANY of the listed values (logical OR). Draft statuses (DRAFT_*) can match unless include_drafts=False. Allowed values:
- `DRAFT_PARSING`: The draft bill is being parsed (e.g., via OCR).
- `DRAFT_MISSING_INFO`: The draft bill is missing required information.
- `DRAFT_READY`: The draft bill is ready to be submitted as a bill.
- `DRAFT_QUEUED`: The draft bill is queued for automatic conversion to a bill upon vendor approval.
- `APPROVAL_PENDING`: The bill is waiting for one or more approvals.
- `AWAITING_RELEASE`: The bill is waiting for payment release.
- `PAYMENT_READY`: The bill is ready for payment.
- `PAYMENT_ERROR`: The bill payment failed.
- `ON_HOLD`: The bill has been placed on hold.
- `BLOCKED`: The bill is blocked from payment initiation or approval.
- `HELD_BY_PROVIDER`: The bill payment is held by the payment provider.
- `PENDING_VENDOR_APPROVAL`: The bill is waiting for a vendor edit to be approved.
- `PAYMENT_DETAILS_MISSING`: The bill is missing required payment details.
- `PAYMENT_NOT_INSTRUCTED`: The bill uses Ramp payments but has not been scheduled yet.
- `WAITING_FOR_TRANSACTION_MATCH`: The bill is paid by card and is waiting for a matching card transaction.
- `WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER_MATCH`: The bill is paid by direct debit and is waiting for a matching wallet transfer.
- `WAITING_FOR_VENDOR`: The bill is waiting on required vendor information.
- `AWAITING_PAYMENT`: The bill is waiting for the business to send push-payment funding.
- `PAYMENT_PROCESSING`: The bill payment has been initiated and is processing.
- `PAYMENT_SCHEDULED`: The bill payment is scheduled.
- `PAYMENT_COMPLETED`: The bill has been paid.
- `ARCHIVED`: The bill has been archived.
- `APPROVAL_REJECTED`: The bill was rejected in the approval flow.

to_payment_date.title: to_payment_date
to_payment_date.description: Inclusive upper bound on the date a bill was paid (payment sent date). Use with from_payment_date to find bills paid within a date range.

name: ramp_search_flight_modifications
description:
Search replacement flights for an existing booking.

Identify the booking with exactly one booking identifier field and leave the
others null; passing several IDs for the same booking is rejected.

First inspect the booking itinerary and ask which leg, date, or route the
traveler wants to change. Pass one entry per changed leg, identified by its
0-based ``leg_index``. Unspecified date and airport fields retain the
original leg values, so an entry with only ``leg_index`` searches that leg
on its booked date and route: use it for a same-day earlier or later flight
(with a departure or arrival time window) or a cabin change (with
``cabin_class``).

When changing both legs of a single-ticket round trip, first search with both
leg modifications, present the outbound offers, then call again with the
chosen ``selected_outbound_offer_id`` and the same modifications to retrieve
matching returns. Split-ticket bookings change one leg per exchange: when
several legs are passed, only the earliest requested leg is searched and
``deferred_leg_indexes`` lists the others to change afterwards in their own
searches. ``selected_outbound_offer_id`` is rejected for split-ticket bookings.

Some bookings support the first search but not this second step, and return an
unsupported-provider result with support details; route the traveler to that
support rather than retrying. Search prices are estimates; call
SubmitFlightModification to re-quote the selected offer with the airline before
asking the traveler to confirm.

``recommended_offers`` is always present, ranked from this page of ``offers``;
each surface presents those entries in the format it supports, and
``assistant_note`` states which presentation applies.

Preference fields (``cabin_class``, ``max_stops``, ``airlines``, timing
windows, ``avoid_red_eye_flights``) become this booking's cumulative
modification preference state: they carry across the outbound and return
steps and later re-searches of the same booking. Omitted preferences retain
their prior values; use ``clear_preferences`` only when the traveler removes
one. ``applied_preferences`` reports what each response used.

airlines.title: airlines
airlines.description: Airline IATA codes to rank higher (e.g. ['AA', 'DL']). Ranks replacements only and never filters them, because exchange inventory is narrow. Retained for this booking's later calls.

avoid_red_eye_flights.title: avoid_red_eye_flights
avoid_red_eye_flights.description: Preference to avoid red-eye replacements for this modification. This ranks and explains recommendations only; it does not save a traveler preference.

booking_id.title: booking_id

booking_request_id.title: booking_request_id

clear_preferences.title: clear_preferences

preferred_arrival_time_window.title: preferred_arrival_time_window

name: ramp_search_flights
description:
Searches flights for a route and dates. Returns policy-tagged offers, or a job_id while the search is still running. To book, use the selected offer's id.

Pass either route fields or job_id, not both. A job_id call reads the existing search without starting a new one. Round trips return outbound offers first; pass job_id with outbound_offer_id to get matching return offers. Preferences persist on the job until changed or cleared. Does not modify existing bookings.

Flight credits, only when the business has flight credits enabled: an offer whose booked fare may accept one of the traveler's credits has airline_credit_eligible=true and the largest such credit, with its currency, in top_airline_credit; each fare option lists its own eligible_credit_ids. only_airline_credit_eligible=true keeps only flights with such a fare and fails with AIRLINE_CREDIT_FILTER_UNAVAILABLE when credits are not enabled or the traveler has no credit Ramp Travel can apply. Eligibility is not a guarantee; the airline confirms it only when the credit is applied to a flight quote.

additional_arrivals.title: additional_arrivals
additional_arrivals.description: Other arrival locations searched together with arrival, in the same formats (e.g. ['EWR']). For a round trip, the return may leave from any listed arrival and land at any listed departure. Same rules as additional_departures.

additional_departures.title: additional_departures
additional_departures.description: Other departure locations searched together with departure, in the same formats (e.g. ['OAK', 'SJC']). A city already covers its own airports. Requires departure; rejected with MULTI_AIRPORT_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE when this traveler cannot search several locations.

airlines.title: airlines
airlines.description: Hard filter: only return these airline IATA codes (e.g. ['AA', 'DL']).

arrival.title: arrival
arrival.description: Arrival airport IATA code, Ramp city search_code, or city, metro, or airport name (e.g. 'NYC', 'Boston Logan').

avoid_red_eye_flights.title: avoid_red_eye_flights
avoid_red_eye_flights.description: Ranks red-eye flights lower in this search's recommendations. Does not save a traveler preference.

cabin_class.title: cabin_class
cabin_class.description: One cabin or a list of cabins searched together: ECONOMY, PREMIUM_ECONOMY, BUSINESS, or FIRST. If omitted, recommendations use the highest in-policy cabin unless a saved cabin preference applies. On a return-offer read, each itinerary uses its cheapest match among the requested cabins.

clear_preferences.title: clear_preferences
clear_preferences.description: Preference names to remove from this job's saved preferences. Requires job_id and cannot include a field that also has a new value. Timing clears apply to the current leg; return_preferred_* names clear saved return timing.

cursor.title: cursor
cursor.description: Opaque page cursor: a completed response's next_cursor, or current_page_cursor to replay the current page. Requires job_id; re-send the same filters, sort_key, and outbound_offer_id.

departure.title: departure
departure.description: Departure airport IATA code, Ramp city search_code, or city, metro, or airport name (e.g. 'NYC', 'Boston Logan'). If omitted on a new search, defaults to the traveler's saved home city, then their most frequent departure city across their flight bookings.

departure_date.title: departure_date
departure_date.description: Outbound date (YYYY-MM-DD). Required for a new search.

include_fare_options.title: include_fare_options
include_fare_options.description: Also return each flight's alternative fare classes in fare_options (e.g. Economy Plus, Business).

include_recommendations.title: include_recommendations
include_recommendations.description: If false, returns the ranked offers page without recommendations.

job_id.title: job_id
job_id.description: ID of an existing search, from a previous response. Use it to get results, page, re-rank, or fetch return flights. Omit it to start a new search.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Maximum offers to return (1-100). Defaults to 20. Output is token-capped, so large limits may return fewer offers; paginate with next_cursor for more.

max_stops.title: max_stops
max_stops.description: Hard maximum-stop filter: 0 for nonstop, 1 for at most one stop, etc.

only_airline_credit_eligible.title: only_airline_credit_eligible
only_airline_credit_eligible.description: True keeps only flights with a fare that may accept one of the traveler's flight credits that Ramp Travel can apply. That fare may not be the one the offer's id books. Applies to this call only; re-send it with cursor. Rejected with AIRLINE_CREDIT_FILTER_UNAVAILABLE when flight credits are unavailable in this booking flow or the traveler holds no such credit.

only_split_tickets.title: only_split_tickets
only_split_tickets.description: Filter results to split-ticket (multi-ticket) fares only. True returns only fares where ticket_type is multi_ticket; False returns only single_ticket fares. Null (default) returns both.

outbound_offer_id.title: outbound_offer_id
outbound_offer_id.description: Outbound offer id, used with job_id to fetch matching return offers. A nested fare option's id may be passed as outbound_offer_id to preserve its cabin and fare on the returns; this needs include_fare_options=true. The chosen return offer's id books the full itinerary.

preferred_airlines.title: preferred_airlines
preferred_airlines.description: Soft preference as airline IATA codes (e.g. ['UA']). Ranks matching flights higher without excluding other airlines.

preferred_arrival_time_window.title: preferred_arrival_time_window
preferred_arrival_time_window.description: Arrival time preference for the current leg, such as morning, afternoon, or evening. On an outbound_offer_id read, it applies to return offers.

preferred_connectivity.title: preferred_connectivity
preferred_connectivity.description: Soft preference for 'wifi' or 'starlink'. preferred_departure_time_window.description: Departure time preference for the current leg, such as morning, afternoon, or evening. On an outbound_offer_id read, it applies to return offers.

Search Ramp's authoritative Help Center documentation for product knowledge and guidance for users.

exclude_article_keys.title: exclude_article_keys

Each parallel call uses all keys known before its batch; add new keys before the next batch. Rewording or changing subtopics does not reset exclusions; only a new user intent does. name: ramp_search_hotel
description:
Search hotels using the canonical Ramp web inventory and policy flow. Before first use in a conversation, load and follow the ramp-book-hotel skill when available.

Provide location_query (city, neighborhood, address, or landmark) plus check_in_date and check_out_date. location_query text containing 'office', 'HQ', or 'headquarters' is rejected unless latitude and longitude are also passed; to search near an office without coordinates, pass its street address as location_query. API calls run synchronously by default and return ranked hotels - each with at most one summary rate - plus policy_summary, total_count, and web_search_url. Results are paginated from a cached result set: pass the returned next_cursor as cursor to fetch more hotels without triggering a new provider search; never construct or edit a cursor. Put chain requests in filters.chain_names and reserve hotel_name for one exact property; a specific hotel_name uses the targeted direct-hotel path. Passing wait_for_results=false explicitly opts into an asynchronous kickoff that returns status='searching' with a search_id to resume by passing that search_id on a later call.

To book from these results, pass the selected hotel id to GetHotelRates, then the selected rate id to SubmitHotelBooking with the same traveler and stay dates.

description: Search for purchase orders using structured purchase order filters.

blanket_purchase_order_id.description: purchase_order_id of a blanket PO. Returns only the release POs ordered against it.

is_blanket_purchase_order.description: True returns only blanket POs; False excludes them. Omit to return both.

payee_uuids.description: Exact vendor or payee UUIDs. Use this for vendor/payee queries after resolving the vendor. Omit this field unless you have at least one UUID; do not pass an empty list for no payee filter.

items.description:
Describes the status of a PurchaseOrder that we display to users

A PO created in Ramp can have the following statuses:
- OPEN
- PARTIALLY_BILLED
- FULLY_BILLED
- CLOSED

An Imported PO can have the following statuses:
- OPEN
- FULLY_BILLED
- CLOSED
- DELETED

items.description:
Represents the receipt status of the PO.
A PO is considered to be `FULLY_RECEIVED` if and only if all of the PO line
items have been received.

receipt_statuses.description: Receiving statuses to include. Only purchase orders that track receiving (three-way match) have one, so this filter excludes the rest.

requires_user_action.description: True to only show purchase orders waiting on the acting user. Omit for no action filter.

search.description: Free-text match on PO number, request name, or owner name. For vendor or payee queries, resolve the vendor first and pass payee_uuids.

items.description:
Represents the creation source of a PurchaseOrder.

- RAMP: PurchaseOrder created in Ramp
- ACCOUNTING_PROVIDER: PurchaseOrder imported from an accounting provider
- DEVELOPER_API: PurchaseOrder created via the Developer API
- EXTERNAL_IMPORT: PurchaseOrder imported from a non-accounting external source

sources.description: Creation sources to include. Use ACCOUNTING_PROVIDER for synced ERP/QuickBooks/NetSuite purchase orders, EXTERNAL_IMPORT for externally imported purchase orders, both for imported purchase orders, and RAMP for purchase orders created in Ramp.

spend_request_statuses.description: Underlying spend request statuses to include.

id.description: Tag identifier. Tracking-category tags require an integer option ID or UUID.

type.description:
This enum represents all possible categories of filters that can be applied to a
table search across all of Ramp.

Subsets of these categories are used in different surfaces, such as transactions,
reimbursements, bills, and reporting. The specific subsets used by each surface
is declared below.

The values of these enums are persisted in the database as a part of saved table
views and reports, and thus they should never be renamed or deleted without migrating
all saved table views and reports first, or ensuring that said enums are not
currently being persisted in the database.

Similarly, each surface should not remove any supported categories without ensuring
